title: Adding and subtracting near multiples of 10

beats.say: Open with a playful 'shortcut' hook: 45 + 19 looks awkward but there is a trick, and we will learn it. No questions.

lines.say: Forty-five plus nineteen. Ugh, nineteen is awkward. But nineteen is just one tiny step away from a number we love, and that's the secret.

beats.say: Near multiples of 10: numbers just over or under, ending in 9, 8, 1 or 2. 19 = 20 - 1, 21 = 20 + 1, 29 = 30 - 1. No questions.

lines.say: A near multiple of ten is a number sitting right next to a multiple of ten. Nineteen is just one less than twenty.
Twenty-one is just one more than twenty.
Twenty-nine is one less than thirty, thirty-eight is two less than forty, and thirty-two is two more than thirty.

beats.say: Add 19 by adding 20 and then taking 1 back (compensate). Walk through 45 + 19 = 64. Use a story: pay with a 20 note, get 1 change. No questions.

lines.say: So to add nineteen, I add twenty instead, because twenty is easy, and then I fix it.
Forty-five plus twenty is sixty-five.
But I added one too many, because nineteen is one less than twenty. So I take that one back: sixty-four.

lines.text: Add a bit too much, then take the extra back
lines.say: That fix-up has a name, compensating. Like paying with a twenty-dollar note for something that costs nineteen: you hand over too much, then get one dollar change.

beats.say: A friend adds 20 and then ADDS 1 (45 + 19 = 66). Test with an estimate and show the fix goes the other way. No questions.

lines.say: A friend of mine did the first step the same, adding twenty to get sixty-five. But then they added one more, and said sixty-six.

lines.text: 19 is LESS than 20, so 45 + 19 is less than 65
lines.say: Let's test it. Nineteen is smaller than twenty, so forty-five plus nineteen must be less than forty-five plus twenty. It can't be sixty-six!

lines.text: Added too much → take it BACK
lines.say: We added too much, so the fix is to take away. Always ask: did I add too much or too little?

beats.say: Subtracting 19 and adding/subtracting 21: 63 - 19 = 63 - 20 + 1; 36 + 21 = 36 + 20 + 1; 58 - 21 = 58 - 20 - 1. Explain the direction of the fix each time. No questions.

lines.say: Three more to try, using the same idea: round to twenty, then fix by one.
To subtract nineteen, take away twenty, which is one too many, so give one back. Sixty-three minus twenty is forty-three, plus one is forty-four.
To add twenty-one, add twenty, and then one more, because twenty-one is one more than twenty. Fifty-six, fifty-seven.
To subtract twenty-one, take away twenty, then one more. Thirty-eight, then thirty-seven.

beats.say: Summary rule with direction: 19 or 29 etc: +/-ten then fix opposite; 21 or 31: do the same direction. No questions.

lines.text: Round to the nearby ten, then FIX the difference
lines.say: So the whole trick: round the awkward number to its nearby ten, do the easy sum, then fix the small difference.

lines.text: Rounded UP (19, 29): undo.   Rounded DOWN (21, 31): carry on.
lines.say: If we rounded up, as with nineteen, we fix by going back. If we rounded down, as with twenty-one, we carry on in the same direction.

beats.say: Do one TOGETHER: 52 + 29. Questions written on the board first.

lines.say: Now you help me. Fifty-two plus twenty-nine.
Twenty-nine is one less than thirty, so we'll add thirty.

ask.prompt: 29 is close to which multiple of ten?
ask.onMiss: Ask: what ten is just above 29?

lines.say: Fifty-two plus thirty is eighty-two.
But we added one too many, so one comes back.

ask.prompt: Did we add too much or too little? So what do we do to fix it?
ask.onMiss: Ask: is 29 more or less than 30?

beats.say: The child works alone: 74 - 19; 38 + 21; explain the fix. Hints only if stuck.

lines.say: Your turn to lead. Two sums to do.
First, seventy-four minus nineteen.

ask.prompt: Work out 74 − 19. Tell me your steps.
ask.onMiss: Ask: take away 20 first. Was that too much or too little?

lines.say: Now thirty-eight plus twenty-one.

ask.onMiss: Ask: add 20 first. Is 21 more or less than 20?

lines.text: Check: did I go over or under? Then fix the other way
lines.say: One more idea to remember.

ask.prompt: In your own words: when do we take the extra back, and when do we add on?
ask.lookFor: Take back when we added/took too much (rounded up, like 19); carry on when 21 is more than 20.
ask.onMiss: Ask: is 19 more or less than 20? Is 21?
